title: dynamic-batching-by-sequence-length-bucketing-and-padding-minimization
author: Ravi Menon
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching in the serving runtime currently groups requests by arrival time and model compatibility which can lead to excessive padding when input sequence lengths vary significantly. This PR implements a dynamic batching heuristic that buckets requests by sequence length and minimizes padding within a batch while preserving latency SLOs.

Approach: Introduce a lightweight sequence-length bucketing layer and a bucket-aware scheduler. Buckets are defined by configurable boundaries and a small windowed wait period to allow aggregation. The scheduler picks batches by attempting to fill the target GPU batch size with minimal additional padding tokens; when ideal fill cannot be achieved within the latency window the scheduler falls back to the oldest-first policy to meet SLOs. We also add a padding-minimization pass that reorders compatible KV-cache entries to reduce memory copy overhead.

Key changes: new serving/scheduler/heuristics.py with bucketing logic and boundary autotune hints; serving/scheduler/dynamic_batcher.py implements the bucketed queue, windowing, and the packer; serving/tests/test_dynamic_batcher.py with unit tests covering boundary conditions and SLO enforcement; benchmarks/seqlen-batching/bench_report.csv and README showing throughput/latency results; docs/observability/dynamic-batching.md describing metrics exposed (bucket_fill_ratio, pad_token_overhead, bucket_wait_time); examples/seqlen-batching-config.yaml shows config knobs (bucket_boundaries, latency_window_ms, min_bucket_fill, enable_seqlen_bucketing).

Performance summary: In internal bench runs on a mix of chat workloads (short, medium, long) we observed ~18% average throughput improvement and a 32% reduction in padded tokens per batch for typical web-chat mixes; median latency stayed within the configured SLO and p99 latency regressions were <2% in most cases. We include a regression test that runs the benchmark harness on the perf-canary fleet.

Compatibility and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime config flag "enable_seqlen_bucketing" (default off). Bucketing boundaries are cluster-configurable and an autotune helper outputs suggested splits based on recent sequence-length histograms. There is an explicit kill-switch to revert to time-based continuous batching.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added and bench harness extended. An initial CI run showed a flaky timing-based unit test failure on macOS runners which was fixed by making the test clock deterministic; CI rerun passed all checks.

Notes: This PR focuses on heuristics and correctness; follow-ups will add per-model profile-driven bucket defaults and tighter kernel-padding co-optimizations to further reduce runtime copy overhead.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Nice approach, can we please ensure bucket boundaries are deterministic across restarts? I'd prefer boundaries derived from a persisted histogram snapshot rather than ephemeral in-memory stats.

Ravi Menon: +reply We persist a rolling histogram to the cluster metadata store and the autotune helper seeds the default boundaries from that snapshot. The PR adds persistence hooks in heuristics.py.
Marco Alvarez: Request change: expose a runtime toggle to disable seqlen bucketing per-deployment (we need a safe rollback path).
Ravi Menon: +reply added enable_seqlen_bucketing toggle in examples and runtime config; default is false. Documented rollback in docs/observability/dynamic-batching.md.
Ethan Brooks: Suggestion: add a metric for pad_token_overhead per-batch and a gauge for bucket_fill_ratio. Also please add an integration-level test for SLO enforcement when bucket waits are used.
Ravi Menon: +reply added both metrics and a perf-canary integration job that asserts SLO compliance under a synthetic mix.

release_notes: Added sequence-length bucketing to dynamic batching to reduce padding and improve throughput. Feature gated; default disabled. Includes metrics (pad_token_overhead, bucket_fill_ratio) and an autotune helper for bucket boundaries.
